description: Retrieval-only benchmark for hybrid search (migration 002). Runs directly against match_chunks_hybrid — no generation, no LLM nondeterminism. Each query must retrieve its expected section at rank <= rank_threshold in the RRF-fused results. Seeded with grounded-02's flagship query plus keyword-exact stress queries whose target section is title-anchored (the class vector-only retrieval is blind to). expected_section is the chunk_index, which for the AegisOps manual equals the manual's section number (chunk 0 = summary; chunks 1-20 = sections 1-20).

queries.query: How do I schedule a weekly vulnerability scan?
queries.note: Flagship (grounded-02). Failed vector-only 3 consecutive runs. The stem 'schedul' is right in the title but absent from the embedding-nearest sections. Section 6 does NOT contain the word 'vulnerability' (that lives in section 5), so AND-of-all-terms FTS would exclude it — OR-recall matches schedul|week|scan and ts_rank ranks section 6 top of the lexical channel.

queries.query: How do I suppress noisy alerts?
queries.note: 'Suppress' is title-anchored (section 9: Alert Rules & Suppression). Section 9 lacks the word 'noisy', so OR-recall (suppress|alert) carries it while AND would drop it. Multiple sections mention 'alert' (8, 10) — tests that ts_rank favours the suppression section.

queries.query: How do I deploy a monitoring agent?
queries.note: 'deploy'/'agent' are title-anchored (section 4). 'agent' also appears in sections 8 and 20 (offline-agent troubleshooting), so this tests lexical disambiguation toward the deployment section.

queries.query: Where do I generate a breach report?
queries.note: Exact feature name in the title (section 12). All stems (breach, report, generat) are present — a clean lexical hit that should dominate its FTS rank.

queries.query: How do I set up single sign-on?
queries.note: Exact feature name 'single sign-on' + SSO/SAML/MFA all present in section 14. Distinctive vocabulary that vector search may under-rank against generic 'set up' phrasing.
